**Finding: Deviation (high severity) — Assignment and change of control**

The agreement restricts assignment in two places, both problematic for us:

- **§ 20(d) (p0142)** — mutual, but a flat consent requirement with no reasonableness standard and no affiliate/M&A successor carve-out. That fails the fallback and lands in walk-away territory ("blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out").
- **§ 3(c) (p0033)** — a one-sided use restriction barring Sparkling from assigning the Agreement except as Garman authorises in writing, which would otherwise override any carve-out.

On the positive side, no Vendor change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists: § 17 triggers are limited to Sparkling's 90-day convenience right and insolvency events, and "control" appears elsewhere only in force majeure and IP warranty contexts.

**Redline (validated, preferred position):** § 20(d) now carries a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard, an express right for Sparkling to assign without consent to an affiliate or a merger/asset-sale successor on written notice, a bar on Garman assigning to our competitors, and confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling is neither an assignment nor a Garman termination/re-pricing trigger. § 3(c) is subordinated with "except as permitted by Section 20(d)".
